 Vending Machine Biscuit and Sausage Gravy Meals in Six Southern States Face USDA Listeria Alert Over Recalled Biscuits 
 El USDA emitió una alerta sanitaria para comidas Mmm! Meals de galleta y salsa con salchicha vendidas en seis estados, debido a galletas retiradas por posible contaminación con Listeria.

 Vending Machine Biscuit and Sausage Gravy Meals in Six Southern States Face USDA Listeria Alert Over Recalled Biscuits
 Published Nov 17, 2026 10:18 PM EST 
 By
 Joseph James 
 Editorial Illustration via AI 
 Share on Twitter 
 Share on Facebook 
 Share on WhatsApp 
 The U.S. Department of Agriculture's Food Safety and Inspection Service has issued a public health alert for ready-to-eat meat products that may contain biscuits recalled over possible Listeria contamination , Food Safety News reported . The Nov. 14 alert names 9.5-ounce Mmm! Meals Made in Minutes Biscuit & Sausage Gravy with use-by dates from Nov. 12 through Nov. 18, 2026.
 The meals were sold mainly through vending machines in Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Oklahoma, Tennessee, and Texas, according to a report published by Yahoo News . FSIS said more downstream products may be identified as the biscuit recall continues.
 That warning shifts the concern beyond one product. Shift workers, hospital staff, warehouse crews, and others who grab breakfast from a machine may not know a recall exists, and the list of affected foods could still grow.
 Developing Story Note: This report covers new developments involving the C.H. Guenther & Son biscuit recall and downstream foods. Information may change as authorities release additional findings. Latest verified update: FSIS public health alert issued Nov. 14, 2026, as reported through Nov. 15. 
 The Newly Named Product and Its Labels
 The product comes in clear plastic packaging with a lime-green outline around the label, the Mmm! Meals Made in Minutes logo and the tagline "Just heat & eat." It was distributed by Fresh & Ready Foods LLC of Renton, Washington.
 The problem surfaced when a company told FSIS it had received biscuits recalled by C.H. Guenther & Son of San Antonio, News 4 San Antonio reported . FSIS uses a public health alert when it wants consumers to act but is not requesting a recall. In this case, the meat products contain an FDA-regulated biscuit that its maker had already recalled, and officials said some meals may still be in refrigerators or freezers.
 There have been no confirmed reports of illness from eating the products. FSIS has not said how many meals were distributed.
 A Biscuit Recall That Keeps Widening
 This is the second known downstream product tied to the same biscuits and the first regulated by USDA. Fresh & Ready Foods earlier recalled 2,414 biscuit sandwiches sold in break rooms, cafeterias and refrigerated vending machines in Washington and Oregon, as MedicalDaily previously reported . That recall, announced Nov. 7, did not report any illnesses.
 The new alert moves the issue to a different part of the country. The earlier sandwiches went to the Pacific Northwest, while the gravy meals reached six states across the South, showing that the recalled biscuits traveled further than the first notice suggested.
 Several details remain unconfirmed. C.H. Guenther & Son's own recall had no public FDA notice as of MedicalDaily's earlier report, and neither the company nor regulators have said which biscuit products, how many units, or which other food makers bought them. It is also not known whether Listeria was found in any finished meal or only flagged as a possible risk.
 Listeria Risks for Pregnant Workers and Older Adults
 Listeria can cause serious and sometimes life-threatening infections , and contaminated food may look, smell, and taste normal. Symptoms can appear up to 70 days after eating a contaminated food, so people who ate the product should watch their health for several weeks.
 Healthy adults may have fever, muscle aches, nausea, or diarrhea. In older adults and people with weakened immune systems, the infection can spread beyond the gut, causing headache, stiff neck, confusion, loss of balance, or seizures.
 Pregnancy carries special risk. A pregnant person may feel only mildly ill with fever and aches, while the infection can lead to miscarriage, stillbirth, premature delivery, or a life-threatening infection in the newborn. Pregnant workers should call a clinician even for mild symptoms.
 Freezing does not kill Listeria , so a meal stored in a workplace or home freezer remains a risk. Reheating is not a reliable fix either, because microwaves can heat food unevenly, and FSIS advises consumers not to eat the product at all.
 The people most likely to have bought these meals are workers on early or overnight shifts, including hospital, warehouse, factory, and transit staff, who rely on vending machines when cafeterias are closed.
 Steps for Buyers, Employers and Vending Operators
 Anyone who bought a Mmm! Meals biscuit and sausage gravy should not eat it and should throw it away or return it to the place of purchase. Questions can go to the distributor at 1-855-424-8390 or RecallConcern@HotLineGlobal.com, or to the USDA Meat and Poultry Hotline at 888-MPHotline (888-674-6854).
 Employers and vending operators can check machines and break room freezers for the product, remove it, and post a notice where it was sold, since many buyers will not see a news alert. Refrigerator and freezer shelves that held it can be cleaned with hot, soapy water.
 People in higher-risk groups who ate the meal and develop fever or muscle aches should call a clinician and mention possible Listeria exposure, since a lab test is needed to diagnose it. Most people who eat contaminated food do not become ill, and testing is not recommended for anyone without symptoms.
 Workers who are unsure what they ate can ask the break room manager or vending company which brands were stocked in early and mid-November. Keeping a receipt, a wrapper, or a photo of the label can help a clinician or health department if symptoms appear later.
 FSIS said it will update the alert as more products are identified. MedicalDaily will report any new products, states, or illnesses linked to the recalled biscuits.
 Developing Story Timeline
 Nov. 14, 2026: FSIS issues a public health alert for Mmm! Meals biscuit and sausage gravy sold in six Southern states.
Nov. 10, 2026: MedicalDaily reports the Fresh To You biscuit sandwich recall in Washington and Oregon.
Nov. 7, 2026: Fresh & Ready Foods announces its sandwich recall tied to C.H. Guenther & Son biscuits.

 Key Questions Answered
 What product is affected? 9.5-ounce Mmm! Meals Made in Minutes Biscuit & Sausage Gravy with use-by dates of Nov. 12 through Nov. 18, 2026.
 Where was it sold? Mainly through vending machines in Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Oklahoma, Tennessee, and Texas.
 Why is there a Listeria concern? The meals contain biscuits recalled by C.H. Guenther & Son for possible Listeria contamination.
 Has anyone gotten sick? There have been no confirmed reports of illness.
 Could more products be affected? Yes. FSIS said additional downstream products may be identified.
 What should I do if I ate it? Watch for fever and muscle aches for several weeks, and call a clinician if symptoms appear, especially if pregnant or at higher risk.
